definitions: A simplified representation of a complex electrical system or device using an arrangement of ideal circuit elements (resistors, capacitors, inductors, voltage sources, current sources) that mimics its electrical behavior under specific conditions.

A conceptual tool in electrical engineering and physics used to analyze and predict the performance of real-world components or systems by approximating their electrical characteristics with an idealized circuit.
examples: The battery's equivalent circuit model helped predict its discharge curve.
Engineers developed an equivalent circuit model for the human body to study electrical safety.
Analyzing the transformer required a detailed equivalent circuit model.
